notes: Master list of source categories. Individual knowledge entries may reference these. Do not invent detailed page citations. Human researchers should verify before production academic use.

entries.title: Ibn Hisham — Sirah
entries.summary: Ibn Hisham's redaction of Ibn Ishaq's prophetic biography is a foundational classical Seerah source.
entries.detailed_information: Widely used for early Makkan and Medinan narrative history. Like all early sources, reports vary in chains and detail; critical method is required.
related_questions: How should classical seerah be used carefully?

entries.title: Al-Tabari — History
entries.summary: Al-Tabari's universal history compiles many earlier reports on prophets, the Prophet's life, and early caliphates.
entries.detailed_information: Valuable as a report collection; includes multiple, sometimes conflicting, narrations. Historians treat it as a source anthology requiring critical reading.
entries.historical_significance: Landmark chronicle for early Islamic history.
related_questions: How do historians handle conflicting reports?

entries.title: How this project treats sources
entries.summary: Islamic History AI grounds answers in curated JSON knowledge. AI-generated or hastily compiled historical notes must be reviewed by qualified human researchers before being treated as authoritative.
entries.detailed_information: Source entries may be marked needs_verification. The chatbot must not fabricate citations. College competition demos should clearly disclose that the knowledge base is curated and expandable.
entries.historical_significance: Supports academic honesty and upgrade path for verified scholarship.
related_questions: How do I add new knowledge entries?
